claims.text: LoggingNotifier.Send calls logger.LogInformation("notification for order {OrderId}: {Subject}", orderId, subject) - one message template, two named placeholders, two arguments.

RequestLoggingMiddleware.InvokeAsync calls logger.LogInformation with template "{Method} {Path} responded {StatusCode} in {ElapsedMs}ms" and four arguments: context.Request.Method, context.Request.Path, context.Response.StatusCode, stopwatch.ElapsedMilliseconds.

Microsoft.Extensions.Logging: arguments fill a template's {Name} placeholders by position, not name; each becomes a named property on the log event, which is passed to every registered provider; the console prints it as text, a structured provider can keep values (e.g. JSON "OrderId": 41).
claims.source_hint: .NET docs, Logging in .NET, "Log message template" section (learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/extensions/logging)

claims.text: Live: after login + placing an order, docker logs donhang-api --since 1m (only the last minute) has 'info: DonHang.Infrastructure.LoggingNotifier[0]' then 'notification for order <id>: order placed' (info = LogInformation's label), plus a RequestLoggingMiddleware line per request that minute.

claims.text: When an interpolated string is passed to a parameter of type string, as LogInformation(string? message, params object?[] args) is, the compiler finishes it into one string (typically via String.Format) before the call, so the method never sees the placeholder names or values separately.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference, interpolated string expressions

claims.text: OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync calls notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed") after SaveChangesAsync, unconditionally, so every placed order produces one LoggingNotifier line.

LoggingNotifier's only LogInformation call never includes a StatusCode field, and RequestLoggingMiddleware's only LogInformation call never includes an OrderId field - the two log calls share no field.

claims.text: RequestLoggingMiddleware's LogInformation runs only after 'await next(context)' returns. PlaceOrderAsync throwing ArgumentException, or CancelOrderAsync throwing KeyNotFoundException, skips it; ExceptionHandlingMiddleware, registered before it in Program.cs, catches them and writes the 400/404.

claims.text: Program.cs adds no logging provider; no Serilog/OpenTelemetry/Seq package; appsettings.json sets only LogLevel. So only the host defaults (Console, Debug, EventSource) are registered, and nothing here reads a log event's fields except the console printing them as text.
